original_question: Let V be a germ at 0 of an irreducible complex variety in C^n . For any small enough ǫ > 0, let E = Eǫ := V ∩ Rn ∩ {|z| < ǫ}. Define the extremal function UE on {|z| < ǫ} : UE (z) := sup{u(z); u ≤ 0 on E, 0 ≤ u ≤ 1 on {|z| < ǫ} The problem is to classify those V for which we have a constant A > 0 for which (α) UE (z) ≤ A|ℑz|, |z| < ǫ/2.
target_in_paper: The draft is trying to capture the local Phragmén-Lindelöf classification problem: determine which germs at a real point satisfy the condition now formalized as PLloc, equivalently which real analytic germs are of type PL via complexification. The supplied arXiv item is a problem list rather than a theorem-driven article, so the nearest precise paper-faithful formulation is the PLloc/type-PL formulation in Section 1, especially Definition 1.1 and the surrounding discussion. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9509202))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the local germ setting at the origin, the use of the real trace of the complex variety, the extremal/plurisubharmonic-envelope viewpoint, and the desired linear control by |Im z| near the real point. Those are the essential ingredients of the local Phragmén-Lindelöf problem. ([www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de](https://www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de/~vogt/preprints/Eigene/106.pdf))
missing_details: The paper-faithful formal object is not the unfinished ambient-ball formula in the draft, but the germwise extremal function ω_{a,V}(z) := limsup_{ζ→z} sup{u(ζ) : u plurisubharmonic on V_a, u ≤ 1, u ≤ 0 on X_a}, where X_a = V_a ∩ R^d. ([www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de](https://www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de/~vogt/preprints/Eigene/106.pdf))

The plurisubharmonic functions are taken on the germ/variety V_a itself, not just on the ambient ball B(0, ε), and the upper-semicontinuous regularization limsup_{ζ→z} is part of the definition. ([www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de](https://www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de/~vogt/preprints/Eigene/106.pdf))

The exact comparison notion is germwise domination: ω_a ≺ \tilde{ω}_a means there exists C > 0 such that ω_a ≤ C\tilde{ω}_a in a neighborhood of a on the common variety. PLloc is defined by ω_{a,V} ≺ |Im z|. ([www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de](https://www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de/~vogt/preprints/Eigene/106.pdf))

The paper is formulated at an arbitrary real point a ∈ R^d, not only at 0; the origin is just a special case. ([www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de](https://www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de/~vogt/preprints/Eigene/106.pdf))

Irreducibility is not part of the basic PLloc definition, so your draft is narrower than the paper's formal setup at that point. ([www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de](https://www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de/~vogt/preprints/Eigene/106.pdf))

The draft omits the paper's companion notion: a real analytic germ X_a is of type PL iff its complexification satisfies PLloc. ([www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de](https://www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de/~vogt/preprints/Eigene/106.pdf))

The quantifier 'there exists C > 0 in a neighborhood of a' must be stated explicitly; in the paper this is encoded by the germ order relation rather than by fixing ε/2. ([www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de](https://www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de/~vogt/preprints/Eigene/106.pdf))

The intended research problem is not just to state one inequality for one E_ε, but to characterize/classify germs satisfying PLloc (or type PL) in the germ sense. ([www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de](https://www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de/~vogt/preprints/Eigene/106.pdf))
refined_question: Let V_a be the germ of a complex analytic variety at a real point a ∈ R^d, and let X_a := V_a ∩ R^d. Define the germwise extremal function by ω_{a,V}(z) := limsup_{ζ→z} sup{u(ζ) : u is plurisubharmonic on V_a, u ≤ 1 on V_a, and u ≤ 0 on X_a}. Classify those germs V_a for which ω_{a,V} is dominated near a by the imaginary distance, i.e. for which there exists C > 0 such that ω_{a,V}(z) ≤ C|Im z| for z near a on V_a; equivalently, determine which real analytic germs X_a are of type PL via their complexification. ([www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de](https://www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de/~vogt/preprints/Eigene/106.pdf))
justification: The arXiv item you supplied is identified on arXiv as 'The Several Complex Variables Problem List', i.e. a collection of problems rather than a single theorem/proposition paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9509202)) Your draft matches the local Phragmén-Lindelöf problem in substance, but it is not fully stand-alone and it does not use the paper-faithful formalism. Section 1 of the later precise treatment defines ω_{a,V}, the domination relation ≺, PLloc, and the companion notion 'type PL' for real analytic germs; that is the closest sharp formulation of the question your draft is aiming at. ([www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de](https://www2.math.uni-wuppertal.de/~vogt/preprints/Eigene/106.pdf))
